cues: All twelve tenses fit one grid: three times, past, present and future, by four aspects: simple, continuous, perfect and perfect continuous.
He wrote, was writing, had written, had been writing.
He writes, is writing, has written, has been writing.
He will write, will be writing, will have written, will have been writing.
Learn the signal words too: just, already and yet call for the present perfect; for and since for the perfect continuous; before and by the time for the past perfect.
